messages:
Maya: quick heads-up — onnectar v0.3 embeddings bring-up: I flipped the RNG seed for the augment pipeline and saw recall@1 drop on short queries (<=6 tokens). putting notes here for triage.

Adrian: can you paste the numbers? is this before/after quant?

Maya: before quant: recall@1=0.873, recall@5=0.948. after seed flip (same model float32): recall@1=0.821, recall@5=0.945. that's a notable delta only for short queries. full-query recall almost identical.

Sanjay: interesting — could be ordering sensitivity in minibatch centroids or a nondeterministic knn indexing op. did you rerun multiple seeds?

Maya: reran x3 with different seeds: two seeds stable near 0.87, one seed dropped like above. seems reproducible per-seed. also tried shuffling same seed twice => consistent.

Lin: is the indexing deterministic? which ANN lib did we use for the holdout tests?

Maya: using HNSW with faiss 1.8.4, index built with efConstruction=200, M=32. build is multithreaded (OMP) — maybe thread scheduling interacts with seed-driven sample order.

Adrian: left some notes from past: faiss build can be nondet unless rng/threading fixed. try setting OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 and FAISS_USE_FLOAT16=0 for a deterministic build pass. also check openblas/omp env.

Maya: good call. quick experiment:

```bash
# deterministic build env
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1
export MKL_NUM_THREADS=1
python scripts/build_index.py --dataset holdout_short_queries --seed 1234
```

Maya: with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 and seed=bad-seed, recall@1 recovered to 0.872. so threading nondet is likely culprit.

Sanjay: that narrows it. could still be earlier: our centroid calculation uses np.random.choice for negative sampling during whitening fit. if seed changes sample order, small numerical differences can cascade. but that usually doesn't flip only short queries.

Lin: also confirm embedding postprocessing order (L2 norm clips) — if vector normalization done in a different order across threads you can get tiny FP diffs that push nearest neighbor across decision boundary for short/ambiguous queries.

Maya: I added deterministic flags and reran k-means whitening/train pipeline with OMP forced single-thread; metrics now stable across seeds. but we need a fix that doesn't degrade build perf in CI.

Adrian: plan: 1) make index build deterministic in our eval harness (set OMP_NUM_THREADS=1) so can compare apples-to-apples in PRs 2) instrument and log index build env + seed in test artifacts 3) add a quick CI smoke that reruns a single short-query holdout with two different seeds to detect large seed sensitivity

Maya: created a draft PR with env pin + extra logs: https://ci.internal/r/nectar/1234 (ci-bot will run full sweep)

ci-bot: Build started: nectar-embed-evals/job/1234 — holdout_short_queries, seeds=[42,1337] — logs will be at https://ci.internal/logs/nectar/1234

Adrian: can we also test quantized int8 variant? earlier we saw quant amplified sensitivity.

Maya: ran INT8 per-channel quant (calib set 5k) under deterministic build. results: float32 recall@1 0.872 -> int8 recall@1 0.859 on short queries. delta consistent across seeds when build is deterministic. so quant adds expected small degradation but not seed-conditional issues.

Sanjay: that sounds acceptable; main CV is to avoid nondet flips. for prod code path we should ensure consistent index builds or persist the index artifact from a canonical build step to avoid per-deploy differences.

Lin: +1 on persisting canonical index for each model version. also add a note to the eval playbook: always run short-query holdout and seed-variation check; add an alert when recall@1 drops >0.02 vs baseline.

Maya: filed GH issue: onboarding playbook checklist + canonical index persistence + CI smoke. tagging eng-ml for review. 

Adrian: thanks — this matches what i've seen on other models. small numerical diffs + multithread builds can bite you on short ambiguous queries.

Maya: final note: for next steps i'll: 1) update PR to set deterministic flags only in eval harness (not global runtime) 2) add a small test that runs two seeds and fails CI if recall@1 drop >0.02 3) run a perf pass to measure index build time with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 and document tradeoffs.

Lin: cool. assign me if you want me to own the canonical index artifact pipeline.

Maya: assigning you now. thanks everyone :+1:

deploy-bot: Deployment note: no changes to hosted endpoints. CI-only eval tweak.
